requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.specification: A Wallet Provider SHALL support all Attestation Providers, except possibly if the attestation in question is a Strong User Authentication (SUA) attestation as meant in [Topic 20](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/blob/v2.8.0/docs/annexes/annex-2/annex-2.02-high-level-requirements-by-topic.md#a2313-topic-20---strong-user-authentication-for-electronic-payments) and the Wallet Provider chooses to not support processing of the transactional data associated with that attestation. Except for such cases, Wallet Units SHALL be capable of requesting the issuance of a QEAA, PuB-EAA, or non-qualified EAA from all Attestation Providers at the User's request.
requirements.searchText: issu_33b issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit a wallet provider shall support all attestation providers, except possibly if the attestation in question is a strong user authentication (sua) attestation as meant in [topic 20](./annex-2.02-high-level-requirements-by-topic.md#a2313-topic-20---strong-user-authentication-for-electronic-payments) and the wallet provider chooses to not support processing of the transactional data associated with that attestation. except for such cases, wallet units shall be capable of requesting the issuance of a qeaa, pub-eaa, or non-qualified eaa from all attestation providers at the user's request.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.specification: A Wallet Unit SHALL authenticate and validate the access certificate of the Attestation Provider before requesting the issuance of an attestation. The Wallet Unit SHALL verify that the access certificate is authentic and is valid at the time of validation, and that the issuer of the access certificate is in the Access Certificate Authority LoTE(s), as documented in [Topic 27](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/blob/v2.8.0/docs/annexes/annex-2/annex-2.02-high-level-requirements-by-topic.md#a2316-topic-27---registration-of-pid-providers-providers-of-qeaas-pub-eaas-and-non-qualified-eaas-and-relying-parties).
requirements.searchText: issu_34 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit a wallet unit shall authenticate and validate the access certificate of the attestation provider before requesting the issuance of an attestation. the wallet unit shall verify that the access certificate is authentic and is valid at the time of validation, and that the issuer of the access certificate is in the access certificate authority lote(s), as documented in [[topic 27](./annex-2.02-high-level-requirements-by-topic.md#a2316-topic-27---registration-of-pid-providers-providers-of-qeaas-pub-eaas-and-non-qualified-eaas-and-relying-parties)].

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.specification: Before requesting the issuance of an attestation, the Wallet Unit SHALL verify that the Attestation Provider is a registered QEAA Provider, PuB-EAA Provider, or EAA Provider. To do so, the Wallet Unit SHALL a) Inspect the ``entitlement`` member in the registration certificate of the Attestation Provider, if provided in the Credential Issuer Metadata per ETSI TS 119 472-3 section 4.2.3, and verify the authenticity of the registration certificate. b) If no registration certificate is present, query the responsible Registrar for the registered value of ``entitlement``, using the URI in the Credential Issuer Metadata, if possible. c) If querying the Registrar is not possible, optionally inspect the ``entitlement`` member included in the Credential Issuer Metadata itself per ETSI TS 119 472-3 section 4.2.3. If this procedure does not confirm that the Attestation Provider is indeed registered as a QEAA Provider, PuB-EAA Provider, or EAA Provider, the Wallet Unit SHALL display a warning to the User, and SHALL NOT request the issuance of an attestation.
requirements.notes: The information in the ``entitlement`` member included in the Credential Issuer Metadata (3rd option above) is self-declared by the Attestation Provider. It is up to the Wallet Provider to decide to trust this information if the registration certificate is not available and querying the registry is not successful.
requirements.searchText: issu_34a issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit before requesting the issuance of an attestation, the wallet unit shall verify that the attestation provider is a registered qeaa provider, pub-eaa provider, or eaa provider. to do so, the wallet unit shall a) inspect the ``entitlement`` member in the registration certificate of the attestation provider, if provided in the credential issuer metadata per etsi ts 119 472-3 section 4.2.3, and verify the authenticity of the registration certificate. b) if no registration certificate is present, query the responsible registrar for the registered value of ``entitlement``, using the uri in the credential issuer metadata, if possible. c) if querying the registrar is not possible, optionally inspect the ``entitlement`` member included in the credential issuer metadata itself per etsi ts 119 472-3 section 4.2.3. if this procedure does not confirm that the attestation provider is indeed registered as a qeaa provider, pub-eaa provider, or eaa provider, the wallet unit shall display a warning to the user, and shall not request the issuance of an attestation. the information in the ``entitlement`` member included in the credential issuer metadata (3rd option above) is self-declared by the attestation provider. it is up to the wallet provider to decide to trust this information if the registration certificate is not available and querying the registry is not successful.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.specification: Before requesting the issuance of an attestation, the Wallet Unit SHALL verify whether the Provider properly registered for the issuance of the type of attestation that the User wants to obtain. To do so, the Wallet Unit SHALL a) Inspect the ``providesAttestations`` member in the registration certificate of the Attestation Provider, if provided in the Credential Issuer Metadata per ETSI TS 119 472-3 section 4.2.3, and verify the authenticity of the registration certificate. b) If no registration certificate is present, query the responsible Registrar for the registered value of ``providesAttestations``, using the URI in the Credential Issuer Metadata, if possible. c) If querying the Registrar is not possible, optionally inspect the ``providesAttestations`` member included in the Credential Issuer Metadata itself per ETSI TS 119 472-3 section 4.2.3. If this procedure does not confirm that the Attestation Provider registered for the relevant type of attestation, the Wallet Unit SHALL display a warning to the User, and SHALL NOT request the issuance of an attestation.
requirements.notes: The information in the ``providesAttestation`` member included in the Credential Issuer Metadata (3rd option above) is self-declared by the Attestation Provider. It is up to the Wallet Provider to decide to trust this information if the registration certificate is not available and querying the registry is not successful.
requirements.searchText: issu_34b issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit before requesting the issuance of an attestation, the wallet unit shall verify whether the provider properly registered for the issuance of the type of attestation that the user wants to obtain. to do so, the wallet unit shall a) inspect the ``providesattestations`` member in the registration certificate of the attestation provider, if provided in the credential issuer metadata per etsi ts 119 472-3 section 4.2.3, and verify the authenticity of the registration certificate. b) if no registration certificate is present, query the responsible registrar for the registered value of ``providesattestations``, using the uri in the credential issuer metadata, if possible. c) if querying the registrar is not possible, optionally inspect the ``providesattestations`` member included in the credential issuer metadata itself per etsi ts 119 472-3 section 4.2.3. if this procedure does not confirm that the attestation provider registered for the relevant type of attestation, the wallet unit shall display a warning to the user, and shall not request the issuance of an attestation. the information in the ``providesattestation`` member included in the credential issuer metadata (3rd option above) is self-declared by the attestation provider. it is up to the wallet provider to decide to trust this information if the registration certificate is not available and querying the registry is not successful.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.subsection: D - HLRs for Privacy Risks and Mitigation
requirements.specification: A PID Provider or Attestation Provider SHALL ensure that all unique elements in a PID or attestation have a negligible chance of having the same value across all PIDs or attestations issued by that Provider. This SHALL include at least a) the salt used for hashing every attribute, b) the hash values of all attributes, c) the attestation identifier or index used for revocation purposes (if applicable), d) the attestation public key used for device binding (if applicable), and e) the value of the Attestation Provider signature.
requirements.notes: a) The list of unique elements is based on [ISO/IEC 18013-5] and [SD-JWT VC]. b) This requirement can be achieved, for example, by ensuring that salt values, indexes and attestation identifiers are pseudo-random numbers generated by a cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator (CSPRNG).
requirements.searchText: issu_35 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit a pid provider or attestation provider shall ensure that all unique elements in a pid or attestation have a negligible chance of having the same value across all pids or attestations issued by that provider. this shall include at least a) the salt used for hashing every attribute, b) the hash values of all attributes, c) the attestation identifier or index used for revocation purposes (if applicable), d) the attestation public key used for device binding (if applicable), and e) the value of the attestation provider signature. a) the list of unique elements is based on [iso/iec 18013-5] and [sd-jwt vc]. b) this requirement can be achieved, for example, by ensuring that salt values, indexes and attestation identifiers are pseudo-random numbers generated by a cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator (csprng).

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.subsection: D - HLRs for Privacy Risks and Mitigation
requirements.specification: A Wallet Provider SHALL ensure that all unique elements in a WUA or WIA have a negligible chance of having the same value across all WUAs and WIAs issued by that Wallet Provider. This SHALL include at least a) the attestation identifier or index used for WUa revocation purposes, b) the WUA and WIA public key used for device binding, and c) the value of the Wallet Provider signature over the WUA and WIA.
requirements.notes: a) The list of unique elements is based on [Technical Specification 3](../../technical-specifications/ts3-wallet-unit-attestation.md). b) This requirement can be achieved, for example, by ensuring that indexes are pseudo-random numbers generated by a cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator (CSPRNG).
requirements.searchText: issu_35a issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit a wallet provider shall ensure that all unique elements in a wua or wia have a negligible chance of having the same value across all wuas and wias issued by that wallet provider. this shall include at least a) the attestation identifier or index used for wua revocation purposes, b) the wua and wia public key used for device binding, and c) the value of the wallet provider signature over the wua and wia. a) the list of unique elements is based on [technical specification 3](../../technical-specifications/ts3-wallet-unit-attestation.md). b) this requirement can be achieved, for example, by ensuring that indexes are pseudo-random numbers generated by a cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator (csprng).

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.subsection: D - HLRs for Privacy Risks and Mitigation
requirements.specification: After issuing a PID, attestation, or WUA, a PID Provider, Attestation Provider or Wallet Provider SHALL discard the values of all unique elements, including at least the ones mentioned in requirement ISSU_35 or ISSU_35a (as applicable) above, as well as any timestamps, as soon as they are no longer needed. The Provider SHALL NOT communicate these values to any other party inside or outside the EUDI Wallet ecosystem.
requirements.searchText: issu_35b issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit after issuing a pid, attestation, or wua, a pid provider, attestation provider or wallet provider shall discard the values of all unique elements, including at least the ones mentioned in requirement issu_35 or issu_35a (as applicable) above, as well as any timestamps, as soon as they are no longer needed. the provider shall not communicate these values to any other party inside or outside the eudi wallet ecosystem.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.subsection: D - HLRs for Privacy Risks and Mitigation
requirements.specification: When issuing PIDs, attestations, or WUAs in a batch to a Wallet Unit, a PID Provider, Attestation Provider, or Wallet Provider SHALL ensure that the timestamps in these PIDs, attestations, or WUAs do not enable Relying Parties to conclude that they are part of the same batch (and therefore belong to the same User).
requirements.notes: This can be done, for example, by making timestamps sufficiently imprecise that a high number of batches, each issued to a different Wallet Unit, share the same timestamp values (herd privacy).
requirements.searchText: issu_36 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit when issuing pids, attestations, or wuas in a batch to a wallet unit, a pid provider, attestation provider, or wallet provider shall ensure that the timestamps in these pids, attestations, or wuas do not enable relying parties to conclude that they are part of the same batch (and therefore belong to the same user). this can be done, for example, by making timestamps sufficiently imprecise that a high number of batches, each issued to a different wallet unit, share the same timestamp values (herd privacy).

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.subsection: D - HLRs for Privacy Risks and Mitigation
requirements.specification: A Wallet Provider SHALL ensure that its Wallet Solution supports the following methods for limiting the number of times a User can present the same PID or attestation to Relying Parties: Method A (Once-only attestations, as specified in requirement ISSU_43 - ISSU_47) and Method B (Limited-time attestations, as specified in requirement ISSU_48 - ISSU_50). In addition, a Wallet Provider MAY ensure that its Wallet Solution supports Method C (Rotating-batch attestations, as specified in requirement ISSU_51 - ISSU_54) or Method D (Per-Relying Party attestations, as specified in requirement ISSU_55 - ISSU_57).
requirements.notes: Wallet Solutions, PID Providers, Attestation Providers, and Wallet Providers are free to define and use other methods as well. However, such other methods are out of scope of the ARF.
requirements.searchText: issu_37 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit a wallet provider shall ensure that its wallet solution supports the following methods for limiting the number of times a user can present the same pid or attestation to relying parties: method a (once-only attestations, as specified in requirement issu_43 - issu_47) and method b (limited-time attestations, as specified in requirement issu_48 - issu_50). in addition, a wallet provider may ensure that its wallet solution supports method c (rotating-batch attestations, as specified in requirement issu_51 - issu_54) or method d (per-relying party attestations, as specified in requirement issu_55 - issu_57). wallet solutions, pid providers, attestation providers, and wallet providers are free to define and use other methods as well. however, such other methods are out of scope of the arf.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.subsection: D - HLRs for Privacy Risks and Mitigation
requirements.specification: A PID Provider or Attestation Provider SHALL have a policy describing which of the methods A, B, C, or D, it will use to limit the number of times a Wallet Unit may present a single PID or attestation. For each supported method, the policy SHALL also specify how the values for respective parameters for that method, such as technical validity period and batch size, will be chosen. The goal of the policy SHALL be to ensure that the risk of linkability is mitigated to an acceptable level, given the (expected) usage of the PID or attestation by the User. To determine what an acceptable level of risk is, the PID Provider or Attestation Provider SHALL carry out a risk analysis regarding linkability.
requirements.notes: a) If an Attestation Provider issues multiple attestation types, these requirements apply for each type of attestation separately. b) [Technical Specification 3] specifies that WUAs shall be sent to a PID Provider or Attestation Provider only once. In other words, for WUAs, the use of Method A is mandatory.
requirements.searchText: issu_38 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit a pid provider or attestation provider shall have a policy describing which of the methods a, b, c, or d, it will use to limit the number of times a wallet unit may present a single pid or attestation. for each supported method, the policy shall also specify how the values for respective parameters for that method, such as technical validity period and batch size, will be chosen. the goal of the policy shall be to ensure that the risk of linkability is mitigated to an acceptable level, given the (expected) usage of the pid or attestation by the user. to determine what an acceptable level of risk is, the pid provider or attestation provider shall carry out a risk analysis regarding linkability. a) if an attestation provider issues multiple attestation types, these requirements apply for each type of attestation separately. b) [technical specification 3] specifies that wuas shall be sent to a pid provider or attestation provider only once. in other words, for wuas, the use of method a is mandatory.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.subsection: D - HLRs for Privacy Risks and Mitigation
requirements.specification: PID Providers and Attestation Providers SHALL include the ``credential_reuse_policy`` parameter, specified in section 4.2.4.2 of ETSI 119 472-3, in their Credential Issuer Metadata to specify which of the methods A, B, C, or D the Wallet Unit must use for the PID or attestation issued. Indicated methods SHALL be ordered by preference.
requirements.notes: See also ISSU_40.
requirements.searchText: issu_39 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit pid providers and attestation providers shall include the ``credential_reuse_policy`` parameter, specified in section 4.2.4.2 of etsi 119 472-3, in their credential issuer metadata to specify which of the methods a, b, c, or d the wallet unit must use for the pid or attestation issued. indicated methods shall be ordered by preference. see also issu_40.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.subsection: D - HLRs for Privacy Risks and Mitigation
requirements.specification: Wallet Units SHALL support the ``credential_reuse_policy`` Credential Issuer Metadata parameter specified in section 4.2.4.2 of ETSI 119 472-3 and SHALL present each PID and attestation in accordance with the values set for this parameter by the relevant PID Provider or Attestation Provider.
requirements.searchText: issu_39a issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit wallet units shall support the ``credential_reuse_policy`` credential issuer metadata parameter specified in section 4.2.4.2 of etsi 119 472-3 and shall present each pid and attestation in accordance with the values set for this parameter by the relevant pid provider or attestation provider.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.subsection: D - HLRs for Privacy Risks and Mitigation
requirements.specification: PID Providers and Attestation Providers SHALL indicate in their OpenID4VCI Issuer metadata at least that either method A or method B must be used for a given type of PID or attestation. A PID Provider or Attestation Provider MAY additionally indicate that it prefers using method C and/or method D over method A or method B. In such a case, a Wallet Unit supporting method C and/or method D SHALL use that method, while a Wallet Unit not supporting these methods SHALL use method A or method B, as applicable.
requirements.notes: Example: An Attestation Provider indicates methods {D, C, A} in their metadata, in that order. A Wallet Unit that supports methods C and D (as well as A and B) then uses method D for this type of attestation. A Wallet Unit supporting methods A, B and C uses method C. A Wallet Unit supporting only methods A and B uses method A.
requirements.searchText: issu_40 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit pid providers and attestation providers shall indicate in their openid4vci issuer metadata at least that either method a or method b must be used for a given type of pid or attestation. a pid provider or attestation provider may additionally indicate that it prefers using method c and/or method d over method a or method b. in such a case, a wallet unit supporting method c and/or method d shall use that method, while a wallet unit not supporting these methods shall use method a or method b, as applicable. example: an attestation provider indicates methods {d, c, a} in their metadata, in that order. a wallet unit that supports methods c and d (as well as a and b) then uses method d for this type of attestation. a wallet unit supporting methods a, b and c uses method c. a wallet unit supporting only methods a and b uses method a.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.subsection: D - HLRs for Privacy Risks and Mitigation
requirements.specification: To the maximum extent possible, Wallet Providers, PID Providers, and Attestation Providers SHALL ensure that Users do not notice which of the methods A, B, C, or D is used for their PIDs, attestations, or WUAs.
requirements.searchText: issu_41 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit to the maximum extent possible, wallet providers, pid providers, and attestation providers shall ensure that users do not notice which of the methods a, b, c, or d is used for their pids, attestations, or wuas.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.subsection: D - HLRs for Privacy Risks and Mitigation
requirements.specification: To the maximum extent possible, Wallet Providers, PID Providers, and Attestation Providers SHALL ensure that no User action is needed for the re-issuance of WUAs, PIDs, or attestations.
requirements.notes: For the topic of re-issuance, see also the [Discussion Paper for Topic B](../../discussion-topics/b-re-issuance-and-batch-issuance-of-pids-and-attestations.md).
requirements.searchText: issu_42 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit to the maximum extent possible, wallet providers, pid providers, and attestation providers shall ensure that no user action is needed for the re-issuance of wuas, pids, or attestations. for the topic of re-issuance, see also the [discussion paper for topic b](../../discussion-topics/b-re-issuance-and-batch-issuance-of-pids-and-attestations.md).

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.specification: The Wallet Unit SHALL request the PID Provider or Attestation Provider to issue PIDs or attestations in batches to the Wallet Unit. All PIDs or attestations in a batch SHALL have the same attribute values and the same technical validity period.
requirements.searchText: issu_43 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit the wallet unit shall request the pid provider or attestation provider to issue pids or attestations in batches to the wallet unit. all pids or attestations in a batch shall have the same attribute values and the same technical validity period.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.specification: The Wallet Unit SHALL present each PID or attestation only once to a Relying Party, except when it has fallen back to Method B as specified below, or to another available method.
requirements.searchText: issu_44 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit the wallet unit shall present each pid or attestation only once to a relying party, except when it has fallen back to method b as specified below, or to another available method.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.specification: The Wallet Unit SHALL have a lower limit for the number of unused PIDs or attestations it holds, and SHALL request the issuance of a new batch when this limit is reached. The PID Provider or Attestation Provider SHALL inform the Wallet Unit about the value of the lower limit and the size of the batch to be requested, using the ``credential_reuse_policy`` Credential Issuer Metadata parameter specified in section 4.2.4.2 of ETSI 119 472-3.
requirements.searchText: issu_45 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit the wallet unit shall have a lower limit for the number of unused pids or attestations it holds, and shall request the issuance of a new batch when this limit is reached. the pid provider or attestation provider shall inform the wallet unit about the value of the lower limit and the size of the batch to be requested, using the ``credential_reuse_policy`` credential issuer metadata parameter specified in section 4.2.4.2 of etsi 119 472-3.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.specification: If the Wallet Unit must request a new batch of PIDs or attestations but is not able to do so because it is offline, the Wallet Unit SHALL warn the User that they are about to lose the possibility to present this PID or attestation to a Relying Party and request them to connect their device to the internet.
requirements.searchText: issu_46 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit if the wallet unit must request a new batch of pids or attestations but is not able to do so because it is offline, the wallet unit shall warn the user that they are about to lose the possibility to present this pid or attestation to a relying party and request them to connect their device to the internet.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.specification: If the Wallet Unit has run out of unused PIDs or attestations, but is not able to request a new batch because it is offline, it SHALL fall back to method B (see ISSU_48 - ISSU_50). This means that, when requested by a Relying Party or Attestation Provider, the Wallet Unit SHALL again present one of the already used PIDs or attestations. The Wallet Unit SHALL return to using method A as soon as it is able to go online and request a new batch of PIDs or attestations.
requirements.searchText: issu_47 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit if the wallet unit has run out of unused pids or attestations, but is not able to request a new batch because it is offline, it shall fall back to method b (see issu_48 - issu_50). this means that, when requested by a relying party or attestation provider, the wallet unit shall again present one of the already used pids or attestations. the wallet unit shall return to using method a as soon as it is able to go online and request a new batch of pids or attestations.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.specification: The Wallet Unit SHALL request the PID Provider or Attestation Provider to issue a single PID or attestation to the Wallet Unit.
requirements.searchText: issu_48 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit the wallet unit shall request the pid provider or attestation provider to issue a single pid or attestation to the wallet unit.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.specification: The Wallet Unit SHALL present a PID or attestation multiple times to the same Relying Party or to different Relying Parties, when requested to do so.
requirements.searchText: issu_49 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit the wallet unit shall present a pid or attestation multiple times to the same relying party or to different relying parties, when requested to do so.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.specification: The Wallet Unit SHALL request the PID Provider or Attestation Provider to re-issue a PID or attestation some time before the one existing in the Wallet Unit expires. The PID Provider or Attestation Provider SHALL inform the Wallet Unit about the moment at which the Wallet Unit must request the re-issuance of a PID or attestation (relative to the expiration date of the existing one), using the ``credential_reuse_policy`` Credential Issuer Metadata parameter specified in section 4.2.4.2 of ETSI 119 472-3.
requirements.notes: It is the responsibility of the Relying Party receiving a PID or attestation to validate whether a presented PID or attestation is temporally valid. A Wallet Unit is allowed to present a PID or attestation even if its expiration date is in the past.
requirements.searchText: issu_50 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit the wallet unit shall request the pid provider or attestation provider to re-issue a pid or attestation some time before the one existing in the wallet unit expires. the pid provider or attestation provider shall inform the wallet unit about the moment at which the wallet unit must request the re-issuance of a pid or attestation (relative to the expiration date of the existing one), using the ``credential_reuse_policy`` credential issuer metadata parameter specified in section 4.2.4.2 of etsi 119 472-3. it is the responsibility of the relying party receiving a pid or attestation to validate whether a presented pid or attestation is temporally valid. a wallet unit is allowed to present a pid or attestation even if its expiration date is in the past.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.specification: The Wallet Unit SHALL request the PID Provider or Attestation Provider to issue PIDs or attestations in batches to the Wallet Unit. All PIDs or attestations in a batch SHALL have the same attribute values and the same technical validity period.
requirements.searchText: issu_51 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit the wallet unit shall request the pid provider or attestation provider to issue pids or attestations in batches to the wallet unit. all pids or attestations in a batch shall have the same attribute values and the same technical validity period.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.specification: When a presentation of attributes is requested by multiple Relying Parties, the Wallet Unit SHALL present each PID or attestation in a batch once, in a random order.
requirements.searchText: issu_52 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit when a presentation of attributes is requested by multiple relying parties, the wallet unit shall present each pid or attestation in a batch once, in a random order.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.specification: When all PIDs or attestations in a batch have been presented once, the Wallet Unit SHALL reset the batch, and start presenting each PID or attestation in the batch again in a random order.
requirements.searchText: issu_53 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit when all pids or attestations in a batch have been presented once, the wallet unit shall reset the batch, and start presenting each pid or attestation in the batch again in a random order.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.specification: The Wallet Unit SHALL request the PID Provider or Attestation Provider to re-issue a batch of PIDs or attestations some time before the batch in the Wallet Unit expires. The PID Provider or Attestation Provider SHALL inform the Wallet Unit about the size of the batch and about the moment at which the Wallet Unit must request the re-issuance of a batch (relative to the expiration date of the existing batch), using the ``credential_reuse_policy`` Credential Issuer Metadata parameter specified in section 4.2.4.2 of ETSI 119 472-3.
requirements.searchText: issu_54 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit the wallet unit shall request the pid provider or attestation provider to re-issue a batch of pids or attestations some time before the batch in the wallet unit expires. the pid provider or attestation provider shall inform the wallet unit about the size of the batch and about the moment at which the wallet unit must request the re-issuance of a batch (relative to the expiration date of the existing batch), using the ``credential_reuse_policy`` credential issuer metadata parameter specified in section 4.2.4.2 of etsi 119 472-3.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.specification: The Wallet Unit SHALL present a different PID or attestation to each different Relying Party upon their request. This means that it SHALL comply with Method A for such Relying Parties.
requirements.searchText: issu_55 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit the wallet unit shall present a different pid or attestation to each different relying party upon their request. this means that it shall comply with method a for such relying parties.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.specification: In case a given Relying Party requests attributes from a given type of PID or attestation multiple times, the Wallet Unit MAY present the same PID or attestation to this Relying Party each time. If it does, it SHALL comply with Method B or Method C for such a Relying Party.
requirements.searchText: issu_56 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit in case a given relying party requests attributes from a given type of pid or attestation multiple times, the wallet unit may present the same pid or attestation to this relying party each time. if it does, it shall comply with method b or method c for such a relying party.

requirements.specification: Empty

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.specification: The Wallet Unit SHALL keep track of which PID or attestation it has presented to which Relying Party.
requirements.notes: To do so, the Wallet Unit can use the unique RP identifier from the extension of the presentation request meant in RPRC_19a.
requirements.searchText: issu_57 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit the wallet unit shall keep track of which pid or attestation it has presented to which relying party. to do so, the wallet unit can use the unique rp identifier from the extension of the presentation request meant in rprc_19a.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.subsection: E - HLRs for re-issuance and batch issuance of PIDs and attestations
requirements.specification: A Wallet Unit SHALL give its User the option to manually initiate a re-issuance process for any of the PIDs or attestations in their Wallet Unit.
requirements.notes: This requirement does not apply for WUAs, since Users must not be involved in the management of WUAs.
requirements.searchText: issu_58 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit a wallet unit shall give its user the option to manually initiate a re-issuance process for any of the pids or attestations in their wallet unit. this requirement does not apply for wuas, since users must not be involved in the management of wuas.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.subsection: E - HLRs for re-issuance and batch issuance of PIDs and attestations
requirements.specification: After a successful re-issuance, a Wallet Unit SHALL compare the attribute values of the re-issued PID or attestation with those of the existing PID or attestation, and SHALL notify the User in case of any differences.
requirements.notes: This requirement does not apply for WUAs, since Users must not be involved in the management of WUAs.
requirements.searchText: issu_59 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit after a successful re-issuance, a wallet unit shall compare the attribute values of the re-issued pid or attestation with those of the existing pid or attestation, and shall notify the user in case of any differences. this requirement does not apply for wuas, since users must not be involved in the management of wuas.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.subsection: E - HLRs for re-issuance and batch issuance of PIDs and attestations
requirements.specification: A Wallet Unit SHALL gracefully handle situations in which re-issuance of a PID, attestation, or WUA is refused by the PID Provider, Attestation Provider, or Wallet Provider,for example by attempting a retry after an appropriate delay.
requirements.searchText: issu_60 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit a wallet unit shall gracefully handle situations in which re-issuance of a pid, attestation, or wua is refused by the pid provider, attestation provider, or wallet provider,for example by attempting a retry after an appropriate delay.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.subsection: E - HLRs for re-issuance and batch issuance of PIDs and attestations
requirements.specification: A Wallet Unit SHALL support PID or attestation first-time batch issuance with a single User authentication, regardless of the size of the batch.
requirements.notes: a) See also requirement WIAM_14. b) This requirement does not apply for WUAs, since Users must not be involved in the management of WUAs.
requirements.searchText: issu_61 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit a wallet unit shall support pid or attestation first-time batch issuance with a single user authentication, regardless of the size of the batch. a) see also requirement wiam_14. b) this requirement does not apply for wuas, since users must not be involved in the management of wuas.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.subsection: E - HLRs for re-issuance and batch issuance of PIDs and attestations
requirements.specification: If a PID or attestation was successfully re-issued because the value of one or more of its attributes was changed (including attributes being added or deleted), a Wallet Unit SHOULD delete the correct pre-existing PID or attestation.
requirements.notes: a) It is up to the Wallet Unit, possibly using metadata provided by the PID Provider or Attestation Provider using the [OpenID4VCI] protocol, to determine the PID or attestation to be deleted. b) Additionally, per requirement VCR_09, the PID Provider or Attestation Provider revokes the pre-existing PID or attestation.
requirements.searchText: issu_62 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit if a pid or attestation was successfully re-issued because the value of one or more of its attributes was changed (including attributes being added or deleted), a wallet unit should delete the correct pre-existing pid or attestation. a) it is up to the wallet unit, possibly using metadata provided by the pid provider or attestation provider using the [openid4vci] protocol, to determine the pid or attestation to be deleted. b) additionally, per requirement vcr_09, the pid provider or attestation provider revokes the pre-existing pid or attestation.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.subsection: E - HLRs for re-issuance and batch issuance of PIDs and attestations
requirements.specification: PID Providers and Attestation Providers, and Wallet Units SHALL support the features of [OpenID4VCI] enabling the re-issuance of PIDs and attestations.
requirements.searchText: issu_63 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit pid providers and attestation providers, and wallet units shall support the features of [openid4vci] enabling the re-issuance of pids and attestations.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.subsection: E - HLRs for re-issuance and batch issuance of PIDs and attestations
requirements.specification: PID Providers, Attestation Providers, and Wallet Units SHALL support the features of [OpenID4VCI] enabling the batch issuance of PIDs or attestations.
requirements.searchText: issu_64 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit pid providers, attestation providers, and wallet units shall support the features of [openid4vci] enabling the batch issuance of pids or attestations.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.subsection: E - HLRs for re-issuance and batch issuance of PIDs and attestations
requirements.specification: A PID Provider or an Attestation Provider of device-bound attestations SHALL verify that a re-issued PID or device-bound attestation is issued to the same Wallet Unit as the existing PID or attestation.
requirements.notes: A PID Provider or Attestation Provider can do so by issuing a refresh token to the Wallet Instance during the original issuance of the PID or attestation, and requiring that the Wallet Instance uses it to obtain a fresh access token during re-issuance; see [OpenID4VCI] section 14.5. The PID Provider or Attestation Provider needs to be able to trust that the Wallet Instance handles the refresh tokens in a secure way, so that an attacker cannot use them from another Wallet Instance. This requires trust in the (continued) security and integrity of both the original Wallet Instance and the other Wallet Instance. This trust is provided by providing the PID Provider or Attestation Provider with a valid WUA for the new Wallet Unit during re-issuance, and by enabling the PID Provider or Attestation Provider to verify that the existing Wallet Unit has not been revoked.
requirements.searchText: issu_65 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit a pid provider or an attestation provider of device-bound attestations shall verify that a re-issued pid or device-bound attestation is issued to the same wallet unit as the existing pid or attestation. a pid provider or attestation provider can do so by issuing a refresh token to the wallet instance during the original issuance of the pid or attestation, and requiring that the wallet instance uses it to obtain a fresh access token during re-issuance; see [openid4vci] section 14.5. the pid provider or attestation provider needs to be able to trust that the wallet instance handles the refresh tokens in a secure way, so that an attacker cannot use them from another wallet instance. this requires trust in the (continued) security and integrity of both the original wallet instance and the other wallet instance. this trust is provided by providing the pid provider or attestation provider with a valid wua for the new wallet unit during re-issuance, and by enabling the pid provider or attestation provider to verify that the existing wallet unit has not been revoked.

requirements.subsection: E - HLRs for attestation-signing certificate profiles and certificate policies
requirements.specification: A PID Provider SHALL have a policy governing all aspects of PID issuance and management. The policy SHALL comply with at least the extended normalised certificate policy (‘NCP+’) requirements as specified in ETSI EN 319 411-1, insofar applicable for the issuance of PIDs rather than public key certificates.
requirements.notes: A common dedicated policy for issuing PIDs may be developed in the future. If so, this requirement will be changed to refer to it.
requirements.searchText: issu_67 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit a pid provider shall have a policy governing all aspects of pid issuance and management. the policy shall comply with at least the extended normalised certificate policy (‘ncp+’) requirements as specified in etsi en 319 411-1, insofar applicable for the issuance of pids rather than public key certificates. a common dedicated policy for issuing pids may be developed in the future. if so, this requirement will be changed to refer to it.

requirements.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
requirements.subsection: E - HLRs for attestation-signing certificate profiles and certificate policies
requirements.specification: PID Providers SHALL ensure that the certificates they use for signing PIDs comply with all applicable requirements in ETSI TS 119 412-6, in particular Clause 4.
requirements.searchText: issu_68 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit pid providers shall ensure that the certificates they use for signing pids comply with all applicable requirements in etsi ts 119 412-6, in particular clause 4.

requirements.subsection: E - HLRs for attestation-signing certificate profiles and certificate policies
requirements.specification: A QEAA Provider SHALL have a policy governing all aspects of QEAA issuance and management. The policy SHALL comply with at least the policy for qualified certificates issued to a natural person where the private key and the related certificate reside on a QSCD (‘QCP-n-qscd’) or qualified certificates issued to a legal person where the private key and the related certificate reside on a QSCD (‘QCP-l-qscd’) requirements as specified in ETSI EN 319 411-2, insofar applicable for the issuance of QEAAs rather than public key certificates.
requirements.notes: A common dedicated policy for issuing QEAAs may be developed in the future. If so, this requirement will be changed to refer to it.
requirements.searchText: issu_69 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit a qeaa provider shall have a policy governing all aspects of qeaa issuance and management. the policy shall comply with at least the policy for qualified certificates issued to a natural person where the private key and the related certificate reside on a qscd (‘qcp-n-qscd’) or qualified certificates issued to a legal person where the private key and the related certificate reside on a qscd (‘qcp-l-qscd’) requirements as specified in etsi en 319 411-2, insofar applicable for the issuance of qeaas rather than public key certificates. a common dedicated policy for issuing qeaas may be developed in the future. if so, this requirement will be changed to refer to it.

requirements.subsection: E - HLRs for attestation-signing certificate profiles and certificate policies
requirements.specification: QEAA Providers SHALL ensure that the certificates they use for signing QEAAs comply with all applicable requirements in ETSI TS 119 412-6, in particular Clause 7.
requirements.searchText: issu_70 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit qeaa providers shall ensure that the certificates they use for signing qeaas comply with all applicable requirements in etsi ts 119 412-6, in particular clause 7.

requirements.subsection: E - HLRs for attestation-signing certificate profiles and certificate policies
requirements.specification: Providers of non-qualified EAAs SHALL ensure that the certificates they use for signing EAAs comply with all applicable requirements in ETSI TS 119 412-6, in particular Clause 6.
