AS-AP-10-029.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-029.specification: A PID Provider SHALL sign its Credential Issuer metadata as specified in section 12.2.3 of [OpenID4VCI]. To do so, the PID Provider SHALL use the private key corresponding to the public key in its access certificate. The PID Provider SHALL include its access certificate, as well as all intermediate certificate(s) leading up to the trust anchor of the corresponding Access Certificate Authority (see ISSU_33) in the LoTE, in the ``x5c`` parameter in the JOSE header of the JSON Web Signature for the metadata.
AS-AP-10-029.searchText: issu_22 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit a pid provider shall sign its credential issuer metadata as specified in section 12.2.3 of [openid4vci]. to do so, the pid provider shall use the private key corresponding to the public key in its access certificate. the pid provider shall include its access certificate, as well as all intermediate certificate(s) leading up to the trust anchor of the corresponding access certificate authority (see issu_33) in the lote, in the ``x5c`` parameter in the jose header of the json web signature for the metadata.

AS-AP-10-030.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-030.searchText: issu_22a issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit empty

AS-AP-10-031.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-031.searchText: issu_22b issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit empty

AS-AP-10-032.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-032.specification: For the verification of a PID Provider's access certificates, a Wallet Unit SHALL accept the trust anchors in the LoTE(s) of Access Certificate Authorities it needs.
AS-AP-10-032.notes: a) Access Certificate Authority LoTEs are explained in [Topic 27](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/blob/v2.8.0/docs/annexes/annex-2/annex-2.02-high-level-requirements-by-topic.md#a2316-topic-27---registration-of-pid-providers-providers-of-qeaas-pub-eaas-and-non-qualified-eaas-and-relying-parties).
AS-AP-10-032.searchText: issu_23 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit for the verification of a pid provider's access certificates, a wallet unit shall accept the trust anchors in the lote(s) of access certificate authorities it needs. a) access certificate authority lotes are explained in [[topic 27](./annex-2.02-high-level-requirements-by-topic.md#a2316-topic-27---registration-of-pid-providers-providers-of-qeaas-pub-eaas-and-non-qualified-eaas-and-relying-parties)].

AS-AP-10-033.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-033.specification: A Wallet Provider SHALL support at least one PID Provider, meaning that its Wallet Units SHALL be capable of requesting the issuance of a PID from these PID Provider(s), and that the Wallet Provider has agreed with the PID Provider(s) that the PID Provider(s) will process such a request according to the agreed rules and procedures.
AS-AP-10-033.searchText: issu_23a issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit a wallet provider shall support at least one pid provider, meaning that its wallet units shall be capable of requesting the issuance of a pid from these pid provider(s), and that the wallet provider has agreed with the pid provider(s) that the pid provider(s) will process such a request according to the agreed rules and procedures.

AS-AP-10-034.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-034.specification: Prior to or during installation of a Wallet Instance, the Wallet Provider SHALL notify the User about the PID Provider(s) that are supported by the Wallet Unit.
AS-AP-10-034.searchText: issu_23b issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit prior to or during installation of a wallet instance, the wallet provider shall notify the user about the pid provider(s) that are supported by the wallet unit.

AS-AP-10-035.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-035.specification: A Wallet Unit SHALL authenticate and validate the access certificate of the PID Provider before requesting the issuance of a PID. The Wallet Unit SHALL verify that the access certificate is authentic and is valid at the time of validation, and that the issuer of the access certificate is included in an Access Certificate Authority LoTE.
AS-AP-10-035.searchText: issu_24 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit a wallet unit shall authenticate and validate the access certificate of the pid provider before requesting the issuance of a pid. the wallet unit shall verify that the access certificate is authentic and is valid at the time of validation, and that the issuer of the access certificate is included in an access certificate authority lote.

AS-AP-10-036.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-036.specification: Before requesting the issuance of an attestation, the Wallet Unit SHALL verify that the PID Provider is indeed a registered PID Provider. To do so, the Wallet Unit SHALL a) Inspect the ``entitlement`` member in the registration certificate of the PID Provider, if provided in the Credential Issuer Metadata per ETSI TS 119 472-3 section 4.2.3, and verify the authenticity of the registration certificate. b) If no registration certificate is present, query the responsible Registrar for the registered value of ``entitlement``, using the URI in the Credential Issuer Metadata, if possible. c) If querying the Registrar is not possible, optionally inspect the ``entitlement`` member included in the Credential Issuer Metadata itself per ETSI TS 119 472-3 section 4.2.3. If this procedure does not confirm that the PID Provider is indeed registered as a PID Provider, the Wallet Unit SHALL display a warning to the User, and SHALL NOT request the issuance of a PID.
AS-AP-10-036.notes: The information in the ``entitlement`` member included in the Credential Issuer Metadata (3rd option above) is self-declared by the PID Provider. It is up to the Wallet Provider to decide to trust this information if the registration certificate is not available and querying the registry is not successful.
AS-AP-10-036.searchText: issu_24a issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit before requesting the issuance of an attestation, the wallet unit shall verify that the pid provider is indeed a registered pid provider. to do so, the wallet unit shall a) inspect the ``entitlement`` member in the registration certificate of the pid provider, if provided in the credential issuer metadata per etsi ts 119 472-3 section 4.2.3, and verify the authenticity of the registration certificate. b) if no registration certificate is present, query the responsible registrar for the registered value of ``entitlement``, using the uri in the credential issuer metadata, if possible. c) if querying the registrar is not possible, optionally inspect the ``entitlement`` member included in the credential issuer metadata itself per etsi ts 119 472-3 section 4.2.3. if this procedure does not confirm that the pid provider is indeed registered as a pid provider, the wallet unit shall display a warning to the user, and shall not request the issuance of a pid. the information in the ``entitlement`` member included in the credential issuer metadata (3rd option above) is self-declared by the pid provider. it is up to the wallet provider to decide to trust this information if the registration certificate is not available and querying the registry is not successful.

AS-AP-10-037.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-037.specification: An Attestation Provider SHALL ensure all attestations issued to Wallet Units comply with the requirements specified in the applicable Rulebook, as described in [Topic 12](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/blob/v2.8.0/docs/annexes/annex-2/annex-2.02-high-level-requirements-by-topic.md#a239-topic-12---attestation-rulebooks).
AS-AP-10-037.searchText: issu_25 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit an attestation provider shall ensure all attestations issued to wallet units comply with the requirements specified in the applicable rulebook, as described in [[topic 12](./annex-2.02-high-level-requirements-by-topic.md#a239-topic-12---attestation-rulebooks)].

AS-AP-10-038.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-038.specification: An Attestation Provider SHALL support the OpenID4VCI protocol referenced in ISSU_01 for issuing attestations.
AS-AP-10-038.searchText: issu_26 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit an attestation provider shall support the openid4vci protocol referenced in issu_01 for issuing attestations.

AS-AP-10-039.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-039.specification: An Attestation Provider SHOULD implement device binding for all attestations it issues. If an issued attestation is device-bound, the Attestation Provider SHALL ensure that the attestation is cryptographically bound to a WSCA/WSCD or a keystore available to the Wallet Unit, as specified in [Topic 9](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/blob/v2.8.0/docs/annexes/annex-2/annex-2.02-high-level-requirements-by-topic.md#a236-topic-9---wallet-unit-attestation-and-wallet-instance-attestation).
AS-AP-10-039.notes: a) Device binding is called 'mdoc authentication' in [ISO/IEC 18013-5] and 'key binding' in [SD-JWT-VC]. b) Implementing mdoc authentication is mandatory in [ISO/IEC 18013-5] and therefore, it is mandatory for attestations complying with that standard. c) An Attestation Provider can indicate the desired level of security for the private key storage in its Credential Issuer metadata . See [OpenID4VCI] section 12.2.4 and Appendix D.2. See also WIAM_14b, WIAM_14c, and WUA_05 and WUA_05a.
AS-AP-10-039.searchText: issu_27 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit an attestation provider should implement device binding for all attestations it issues. if an issued attestation is device-bound, the attestation provider shall ensure that the attestation is cryptographically bound to a wsca/wscd or a keystore available to the wallet unit, as specified in [topic 9](./annex-2.02-high-level-requirements-by-topic.md#a236-topic-9---wallet-unit-attestation-and-wallet-instance-attestation). a) device binding is called 'mdoc authentication' in [iso/iec 18013-5] and 'key binding' in [sd-jwt-vc]. b) implementing mdoc authentication is mandatory in [iso/iec 18013-5] and therefore, it is mandatory for attestations complying with that standard. c) an attestation provider can indicate the desired level of security for the private key storage in its credential issuer metadata . see [openid4vci] section 12.2.4 and appendix d.2. see also wiam_14b, wiam_14c, and wua_05 and wua_05a.

AS-AP-10-040.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-040.specification: If the subject of the attestation is a natural person, an Attestation Provider SHALL verify the identity of the subject of the attestation, in compliance with applicable requirements and in accordance with relevant standards or Implementing Regulations.
AS-AP-10-040.notes: Not every attestation has a natural person as its subject. For example, a holiday voucher may be valid for any User that can present it to a Relying Party and therefore has no subject. This is comparable to the concept of a 'bearer token'.

AS-AP-10-041.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-041.specification: If applicable, an Attestation Provider SHALL ensure that the attributes attested in the attestation issued are valid for the identified attestation subject.
AS-AP-10-041.searchText: issu_27b issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit if applicable, an attestation provider shall ensure that the attributes attested in the attestation issued are valid for the identified attestation subject.

AS-AP-10-042.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-042.specification: The Attestation Provider SHALL verify that the User requesting the attestation has the right to receive it.
AS-AP-10-042.searchText: issu_27c issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit the attestation provider shall verify that the user requesting the attestation has the right to receive it.

AS-AP-10-043.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-043.specification: For the verification of a WUA or WIA, an Attestation Provider SHALL accept the trust anchors in the Wallet Provider LoTE.
AS-AP-10-043.notes: The Wallet Provider LoTE is explained in [Topic 31](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/blob/v2.8.0/docs/annexes/annex-2/annex-2.02-high-level-requirements-by-topic.md#a2320-topic-31---notification-and-publication-of-pid-provider-wallet-provider-attestation-provider-access-certificate-authority-and-provider-of-registration-certificates).

AS-AP-10-044.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-044.specification: A QEAA Provider or PuB-EAA Provider SHALL support all Wallet Solutions, except in case the attestation in question is a Strong User Authentication (SUA) attestation as meant in [Topic 20](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/blob/v2.8.0/docs/annexes/annex-2/annex-2.02-high-level-requirements-by-topic.md#a2313-topic-20---strong-user-authentication-for-electronic-payments) and the Wallet Provider does not support processing of the transactional data associated with the SUA attestation. Except for such cases, A QEAA Provider or PuB-EAA Provider SHALL NOT discriminate between Wallet Solutions when processing a request for the issuance of an attestation.
AS-AP-10-044.notes: This requirement is not applicable for non-qualified EAA Providers. For example, a non-qualified EAA Provider may choose to issue attestations in the format specified in [W3C VCDM], see ARB_01a. In that case, it will support only those Wallet Solutions that have implemented this attestation format.
AS-AP-10-044.searchText: issu_29 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit a qeaa provider or pub-eaa provider shall support all wallet solutions, except in case the attestation in question is a strong user authentication (sua) attestation as meant in [topic 20](./annex-2.02-high-level-requirements-by-topic.md#a2313-topic-20---strong-user-authentication-for-electronic-payments) and the wallet provider does not support processing of the transactional data associated with the sua attestation. except for such cases, a qeaa provider or pub-eaa provider shall not discriminate between wallet solutions when processing a request for the issuance of an attestation. this requirement is not applicable for non-qualified eaa providers. for example, a non-qualified eaa provider may choose to issue attestations in the format specified in [w3c vcdm], see arb_01a. in that case, it will support only those wallet solutions that have implemented this attestation format.

AS-AP-10-045.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-045.specification: Before issuing a device-bound attestation, an Attestation Provider SHALL: - verify that the Wallet Provider mentioned in the Wallet Unit's WUA is present in the Wallet Provider LoTE. - authenticate and validate the WUA using the trust anchor(s) registered for the Wallet Provider in that LoTE. - verify that the Wallet Unit's WUA is not revoked.

AS-AP-10-046.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-046.specification: Before issuing an attestation, an Attestation Provider SHALL: - verify that the Wallet Provider mentioned in the Wallet Unit's WIA is present in the Wallet Provider LoTE. - authenticate and validate the WIA using the trust anchor(s) registered for the Wallet Provider in that LoTE.
AS-AP-10-046.notes: This requirement applies to both device-bound and non-device-bound attestations

AS-AP-10-048.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-048.specification: An Attestation Provider SHALL sign its Credential Issuer metadata as specified in section 12.2.3 of [OpenID4VCI]. To do so, the Attestation Provider SHALL use the private key corresponding to the public key in its access certificate. The Attestation Provider SHALL include its access certificate, as well as all intermediate certificate(s) leading up to the trust anchor of the corresponding Access Certificate Authority  in the LoTE (see ISSU_33), in the ``x5c`` parameter in the JOSE header of the JSON Web Signature for the metadata.

AS-AP-10-050.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-050.specification: For the verification of access certificates, a Wallet Unit SHALL accept the trust anchors in all LoTE(s) for Access Certificate Authorities.
AS-AP-10-050.notes: Access Certificate Authority LoTEs are explained in [Topic 27](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/blob/v2.8.0/docs/annexes/annex-2/annex-2.02-high-level-requirements-by-topic.md#a2316-topic-27---registration-of-pid-providers-providers-of-qeaas-pub-eaas-and-non-qualified-eaas-and-relying-parties).

AS-AP-10-051.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-051.specification: For the verification of the registration certificates of Attestation Providers, a Wallet Unit SHALL accept the trust anchors in all LoTE(s) for Providers of registration certificates.
AS-AP-10-051.searchText: issu_33a issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit for the verification of the registration certificates of attestation providers, a wallet unit shall accept the trust anchors in all lote(s) for providers of registration certificates.

AS-AP-10-052.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-052.specification: A Wallet Provider SHALL support all Attestation Providers, except possibly if the attestation in question is a Strong User Authentication (SUA) attestation as meant in [Topic 20](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/blob/v2.8.0/docs/annexes/annex-2/annex-2.02-high-level-requirements-by-topic.md#a2313-topic-20---strong-user-authentication-for-electronic-payments) and the Wallet Provider chooses to not support processing of the transactional data associated with that attestation. Except for such cases, Wallet Units SHALL be capable of requesting the issuance of a QEAA, PuB-EAA, or non-qualified EAA from all Attestation Providers at the User's request.
AS-AP-10-052.searchText: issu_33b issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit a wallet provider shall support all attestation providers, except possibly if the attestation in question is a strong user authentication (sua) attestation as meant in [topic 20](./annex-2.02-high-level-requirements-by-topic.md#a2313-topic-20---strong-user-authentication-for-electronic-payments) and the wallet provider chooses to not support processing of the transactional data associated with that attestation. except for such cases, wallet units shall be capable of requesting the issuance of a qeaa, pub-eaa, or non-qualified eaa from all attestation providers at the user's request.

AS-AP-10-053.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-053.specification: A Wallet Unit SHALL authenticate and validate the access certificate of the Attestation Provider before requesting the issuance of an attestation. The Wallet Unit SHALL verify that the access certificate is authentic and is valid at the time of validation, and that the issuer of the access certificate is in the Access Certificate Authority LoTE(s), as documented in [Topic 27](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/blob/v2.8.0/docs/annexes/annex-2/annex-2.02-high-level-requirements-by-topic.md#a2316-topic-27---registration-of-pid-providers-providers-of-qeaas-pub-eaas-and-non-qualified-eaas-and-relying-parties).
AS-AP-10-053.searchText: issu_34 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit a wallet unit shall authenticate and validate the access certificate of the attestation provider before requesting the issuance of an attestation. the wallet unit shall verify that the access certificate is authentic and is valid at the time of validation, and that the issuer of the access certificate is in the access certificate authority lote(s), as documented in [[topic 27](./annex-2.02-high-level-requirements-by-topic.md#a2316-topic-27---registration-of-pid-providers-providers-of-qeaas-pub-eaas-and-non-qualified-eaas-and-relying-parties)].

AS-AP-10-054.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-054.specification: Before requesting the issuance of an attestation, the Wallet Unit SHALL verify that the Attestation Provider is a registered QEAA Provider, PuB-EAA Provider, or EAA Provider. To do so, the Wallet Unit SHALL a) Inspect the ``entitlement`` member in the registration certificate of the Attestation Provider, if provided in the Credential Issuer Metadata per ETSI TS 119 472-3 section 4.2.3, and verify the authenticity of the registration certificate. b) If no registration certificate is present, query the responsible Registrar for the registered value of ``entitlement``, using the URI in the Credential Issuer Metadata, if possible. c) If querying the Registrar is not possible, optionally inspect the ``entitlement`` member included in the Credential Issuer Metadata itself per ETSI TS 119 472-3 section 4.2.3. If this procedure does not confirm that the Attestation Provider is indeed registered as a QEAA Provider, PuB-EAA Provider, or EAA Provider, the Wallet Unit SHALL display a warning to the User, and SHALL NOT request the issuance of an attestation.
AS-AP-10-054.notes: The information in the ``entitlement`` member included in the Credential Issuer Metadata (3rd option above) is self-declared by the Attestation Provider. It is up to the Wallet Provider to decide to trust this information if the registration certificate is not available and querying the registry is not successful.

AS-AP-10-055.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-055.specification: Before requesting the issuance of an attestation, the Wallet Unit SHALL verify whether the Provider properly registered for the issuance of the type of attestation that the User wants to obtain. To do so, the Wallet Unit SHALL a) Inspect the ``providesAttestations`` member in the registration certificate of the Attestation Provider, if provided in the Credential Issuer Metadata per ETSI TS 119 472-3 section 4.2.3, and verify the authenticity of the registration certificate. b) If no registration certificate is present, query the responsible Registrar for the registered value of ``providesAttestations``, using the URI in the Credential Issuer Metadata, if possible. c) If querying the Registrar is not possible, optionally inspect the ``providesAttestations`` member included in the Credential Issuer Metadata itself per ETSI TS 119 472-3 section 4.2.3. If this procedure does not confirm that the Attestation Provider registered for the relevant type of attestation, the Wallet Unit SHALL display a warning to the User, and SHALL NOT request the issuance of an attestation.
AS-AP-10-055.notes: The information in the ``providesAttestation`` member included in the Credential Issuer Metadata (3rd option above) is self-declared by the Attestation Provider. It is up to the Wallet Provider to decide to trust this information if the registration certificate is not available and querying the registry is not successful.

AS-AP-10-056.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-056.subsection: D - HLRs for Privacy Risks and Mitigation
AS-AP-10-056.specification: A PID Provider or Attestation Provider SHALL ensure that all unique elements in a PID or attestation have a negligible chance of having the same value across all PIDs or attestations issued by that Provider. This SHALL include at least a) the salt used for hashing every attribute, b) the hash values of all attributes, c) the attestation identifier or index used for revocation purposes (if applicable), d) the attestation public key used for device binding (if applicable), and e) the value of the Attestation Provider signature.
AS-AP-10-056.notes: a) The list of unique elements is based on [ISO/IEC 18013-5] and [SD-JWT VC]. b) This requirement can be achieved, for example, by ensuring that salt values, indexes and attestation identifiers are pseudo-random numbers generated by a cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator (CSPRNG).
AS-AP-10-056.searchText: issu_35 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit a pid provider or attestation provider shall ensure that all unique elements in a pid or attestation have a negligible chance of having the same value across all pids or attestations issued by that provider. this shall include at least a) the salt used for hashing every attribute, b) the hash values of all attributes, c) the attestation identifier or index used for revocation purposes (if applicable), d) the attestation public key used for device binding (if applicable), and e) the value of the attestation provider signature. a) the list of unique elements is based on [iso/iec 18013-5] and [sd-jwt vc]. b) this requirement can be achieved, for example, by ensuring that salt values, indexes and attestation identifiers are pseudo-random numbers generated by a cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator (csprng).

AS-AP-10-057.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-057.subsection: D - HLRs for Privacy Risks and Mitigation
AS-AP-10-057.specification: A Wallet Provider SHALL ensure that all unique elements in a WUA or WIA have a negligible chance of having the same value across all WUAs and WIAs issued by that Wallet Provider. This SHALL include at least a) the attestation identifier or index used for WUa revocation purposes, b) the WUA and WIA public key used for device binding, and c) the value of the Wallet Provider signature over the WUA and WIA.
AS-AP-10-057.notes: a) The list of unique elements is based on [Technical Specification 3](../../technical-specifications/ts3-wallet-unit-attestation.md). b) This requirement can be achieved, for example, by ensuring that indexes are pseudo-random numbers generated by a cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator (CSPRNG).
AS-AP-10-057.searchText: issu_35a issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit a wallet provider shall ensure that all unique elements in a wua or wia have a negligible chance of having the same value across all wuas and wias issued by that wallet provider. this shall include at least a) the attestation identifier or index used for wua revocation purposes, b) the wua and wia public key used for device binding, and c) the value of the wallet provider signature over the wua and wia. a) the list of unique elements is based on [technical specification 3](../../technical-specifications/ts3-wallet-unit-attestation.md). b) this requirement can be achieved, for example, by ensuring that indexes are pseudo-random numbers generated by a cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator (csprng).

AS-AP-10-058.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-058.subsection: D - HLRs for Privacy Risks and Mitigation
AS-AP-10-058.specification: After issuing a PID, attestation, or WUA, a PID Provider, Attestation Provider or Wallet Provider SHALL discard the values of all unique elements, including at least the ones mentioned in requirement ISSU_35 or ISSU_35a (as applicable) above, as well as any timestamps, as soon as they are no longer needed. The Provider SHALL NOT communicate these values to any other party inside or outside the EUDI Wallet ecosystem.

AS-AP-10-059.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-059.subsection: D - HLRs for Privacy Risks and Mitigation
AS-AP-10-059.specification: When issuing PIDs, attestations, or WUAs in a batch to a Wallet Unit, a PID Provider, Attestation Provider, or Wallet Provider SHALL ensure that the timestamps in these PIDs, attestations, or WUAs do not enable Relying Parties to conclude that they are part of the same batch (and therefore belong to the same User).
AS-AP-10-059.notes: This can be done, for example, by making timestamps sufficiently imprecise that a high number of batches, each issued to a different Wallet Unit, share the same timestamp values (herd privacy).
AS-AP-10-059.searchText: issu_36 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit when issuing pids, attestations, or wuas in a batch to a wallet unit, a pid provider, attestation provider, or wallet provider shall ensure that the timestamps in these pids, attestations, or wuas do not enable relying parties to conclude that they are part of the same batch (and therefore belong to the same user). this can be done, for example, by making timestamps sufficiently imprecise that a high number of batches, each issued to a different wallet unit, share the same timestamp values (herd privacy).

AS-AP-10-060.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-060.subsection: D - HLRs for Privacy Risks and Mitigation
AS-AP-10-060.specification: A Wallet Provider SHALL ensure that its Wallet Solution supports the following methods for limiting the number of times a User can present the same PID or attestation to Relying Parties: Method A (Once-only attestations, as specified in requirement ISSU_43 - ISSU_47) and Method B (Limited-time attestations, as specified in requirement ISSU_48 - ISSU_50). In addition, a Wallet Provider MAY ensure that its Wallet Solution supports Method C (Rotating-batch attestations, as specified in requirement ISSU_51 - ISSU_54) or Method D (Per-Relying Party attestations, as specified in requirement ISSU_55 - ISSU_57).
AS-AP-10-060.notes: Wallet Solutions, PID Providers, Attestation Providers, and Wallet Providers are free to define and use other methods as well. However, such other methods are out of scope of the ARF.
AS-AP-10-060.searchText: issu_37 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit a wallet provider shall ensure that its wallet solution supports the following methods for limiting the number of times a user can present the same pid or attestation to relying parties: method a (once-only attestations, as specified in requirement issu_43 - issu_47) and method b (limited-time attestations, as specified in requirement issu_48 - issu_50). in addition, a wallet provider may ensure that its wallet solution supports method c (rotating-batch attestations, as specified in requirement issu_51 - issu_54) or method d (per-relying party attestations, as specified in requirement issu_55 - issu_57). wallet solutions, pid providers, attestation providers, and wallet providers are free to define and use other methods as well. however, such other methods are out of scope of the arf.

AS-AP-10-061.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-061.subsection: D - HLRs for Privacy Risks and Mitigation
AS-AP-10-061.specification: A PID Provider or Attestation Provider SHALL have a policy describing which of the methods A, B, C, or D, it will use to limit the number of times a Wallet Unit may present a single PID or attestation. For each supported method, the policy SHALL also specify how the values for respective parameters for that method, such as technical validity period and batch size, will be chosen. The goal of the policy SHALL be to ensure that the risk of linkability is mitigated to an acceptable level, given the (expected) usage of the PID or attestation by the User. To determine what an acceptable level of risk is, the PID Provider or Attestation Provider SHALL carry out a risk analysis regarding linkability.
AS-AP-10-061.notes: a) If an Attestation Provider issues multiple attestation types, these requirements apply for each type of attestation separately. b) [Technical Specification 3] specifies that WUAs shall be sent to a PID Provider or Attestation Provider only once. In other words, for WUAs, the use of Method A is mandatory.

AS-AP-10-062.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-062.subsection: D - HLRs for Privacy Risks and Mitigation
AS-AP-10-062.specification: PID Providers and Attestation Providers SHALL include the ``credential_reuse_policy`` parameter, specified in section 4.2.4.2 of ETSI 119 472-3, in their Credential Issuer Metadata to specify which of the methods A, B, C, or D the Wallet Unit must use for the PID or attestation issued. Indicated methods SHALL be ordered by preference.
AS-AP-10-062.searchText: issu_39 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit pid providers and attestation providers shall include the ``credential_reuse_policy`` parameter, specified in section 4.2.4.2 of etsi 119 472-3, in their credential issuer metadata to specify which of the methods a, b, c, or d the wallet unit must use for the pid or attestation issued. indicated methods shall be ordered by preference. see also issu_40.

AS-AP-10-063.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-063.subsection: D - HLRs for Privacy Risks and Mitigation
AS-AP-10-063.specification: Wallet Units SHALL support the ``credential_reuse_policy`` Credential Issuer Metadata parameter specified in section 4.2.4.2 of ETSI 119 472-3 and SHALL present each PID and attestation in accordance with the values set for this parameter by the relevant PID Provider or Attestation Provider.
AS-AP-10-063.searchText: issu_39a issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit wallet units shall support the ``credential_reuse_policy`` credential issuer metadata parameter specified in section 4.2.4.2 of etsi 119 472-3 and shall present each pid and attestation in accordance with the values set for this parameter by the relevant pid provider or attestation provider.

AS-AP-10-064.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-064.subsection: D - HLRs for Privacy Risks and Mitigation
AS-AP-10-064.specification: PID Providers and Attestation Providers SHALL indicate in their OpenID4VCI Issuer metadata at least that either method A or method B must be used for a given type of PID or attestation. A PID Provider or Attestation Provider MAY additionally indicate that it prefers using method C and/or method D over method A or method B. In such a case, a Wallet Unit supporting method C and/or method D SHALL use that method, while a Wallet Unit not supporting these methods SHALL use method A or method B, as applicable.
AS-AP-10-064.notes: Example: An Attestation Provider indicates methods {D, C, A} in their metadata, in that order. A Wallet Unit that supports methods C and D (as well as A and B) then uses method D for this type of attestation. A Wallet Unit supporting methods A, B and C uses method C. A Wallet Unit supporting only methods A and B uses method A.

AS-AP-10-065.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-065.subsection: D - HLRs for Privacy Risks and Mitigation
AS-AP-10-065.specification: To the maximum extent possible, Wallet Providers, PID Providers, and Attestation Providers SHALL ensure that Users do not notice which of the methods A, B, C, or D is used for their PIDs, attestations, or WUAs.

AS-AP-10-066.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-066.subsection: D - HLRs for Privacy Risks and Mitigation
AS-AP-10-066.specification: To the maximum extent possible, Wallet Providers, PID Providers, and Attestation Providers SHALL ensure that no User action is needed for the re-issuance of WUAs, PIDs, or attestations.
AS-AP-10-066.notes: For the topic of re-issuance, see also the [Discussion Paper for Topic B](../../discussion-topics/b-re-issuance-and-batch-issuance-of-pids-and-attestations.md).

AS-AP-10-067.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-067.specification: The Wallet Unit SHALL request the PID Provider or Attestation Provider to issue PIDs or attestations in batches to the Wallet Unit. All PIDs or attestations in a batch SHALL have the same attribute values and the same technical validity period.

AS-AP-10-068.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-068.specification: The Wallet Unit SHALL present each PID or attestation only once to a Relying Party, except when it has fallen back to Method B as specified below, or to another available method.
AS-AP-10-068.searchText: issu_44 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit the wallet unit shall present each pid or attestation only once to a relying party, except when it has fallen back to method b as specified below, or to another available method.

AS-AP-10-069.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-069.specification: The Wallet Unit SHALL have a lower limit for the number of unused PIDs or attestations it holds, and SHALL request the issuance of a new batch when this limit is reached. The PID Provider or Attestation Provider SHALL inform the Wallet Unit about the value of the lower limit and the size of the batch to be requested, using the ``credential_reuse_policy`` Credential Issuer Metadata parameter specified in section 4.2.4.2 of ETSI 119 472-3.

AS-AP-10-070.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-070.specification: If the Wallet Unit must request a new batch of PIDs or attestations but is not able to do so because it is offline, the Wallet Unit SHALL warn the User that they are about to lose the possibility to present this PID or attestation to a Relying Party and request them to connect their device to the internet.

AS-AP-10-071.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-071.specification: If the Wallet Unit has run out of unused PIDs or attestations, but is not able to request a new batch because it is offline, it SHALL fall back to method B (see ISSU_48 - ISSU_50). This means that, when requested by a Relying Party or Attestation Provider, the Wallet Unit SHALL again present one of the already used PIDs or attestations. The Wallet Unit SHALL return to using method A as soon as it is able to go online and request a new batch of PIDs or attestations.

AS-AP-10-072.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-072.specification: The Wallet Unit SHALL request the PID Provider or Attestation Provider to issue a single PID or attestation to the Wallet Unit.
AS-AP-10-072.searchText: issu_48 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit the wallet unit shall request the pid provider or attestation provider to issue a single pid or attestation to the wallet unit.

AS-AP-10-073.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-073.specification: The Wallet Unit SHALL present a PID or attestation multiple times to the same Relying Party or to different Relying Parties, when requested to do so.
AS-AP-10-073.searchText: issu_49 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit the wallet unit shall present a pid or attestation multiple times to the same relying party or to different relying parties, when requested to do so.

AS-AP-10-074.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-074.specification: The Wallet Unit SHALL request the PID Provider or Attestation Provider to re-issue a PID or attestation some time before the one existing in the Wallet Unit expires. The PID Provider or Attestation Provider SHALL inform the Wallet Unit about the moment at which the Wallet Unit must request the re-issuance of a PID or attestation (relative to the expiration date of the existing one), using the ``credential_reuse_policy`` Credential Issuer Metadata parameter specified in section 4.2.4.2 of ETSI 119 472-3.
AS-AP-10-074.notes: It is the responsibility of the Relying Party receiving a PID or attestation to validate whether a presented PID or attestation is temporally valid. A Wallet Unit is allowed to present a PID or attestation even if its expiration date is in the past.

AS-AP-10-075.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-075.specification: The Wallet Unit SHALL request the PID Provider or Attestation Provider to issue PIDs or attestations in batches to the Wallet Unit. All PIDs or attestations in a batch SHALL have the same attribute values and the same technical validity period.

AS-AP-10-076.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-076.specification: When a presentation of attributes is requested by multiple Relying Parties, the Wallet Unit SHALL present each PID or attestation in a batch once, in a random order.
AS-AP-10-076.searchText: issu_52 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit when a presentation of attributes is requested by multiple relying parties, the wallet unit shall present each pid or attestation in a batch once, in a random order.

AS-AP-10-077.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-077.specification: When all PIDs or attestations in a batch have been presented once, the Wallet Unit SHALL reset the batch, and start presenting each PID or attestation in the batch again in a random order.

AS-AP-10-078.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-078.specification: The Wallet Unit SHALL request the PID Provider or Attestation Provider to re-issue a batch of PIDs or attestations some time before the batch in the Wallet Unit expires. The PID Provider or Attestation Provider SHALL inform the Wallet Unit about the size of the batch and about the moment at which the Wallet Unit must request the re-issuance of a batch (relative to the expiration date of the existing batch), using the ``credential_reuse_policy`` Credential Issuer Metadata parameter specified in section 4.2.4.2 of ETSI 119 472-3.
AS-AP-10-078.searchText: issu_54 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit the wallet unit shall request the pid provider or attestation provider to re-issue a batch of pids or attestations some time before the batch in the wallet unit expires. the pid provider or attestation provider shall inform the wallet unit about the size of the batch and about the moment at which the wallet unit must request the re-issuance of a batch (relative to the expiration date of the existing batch), using the ``credential_reuse_policy`` credential issuer metadata parameter specified in section 4.2.4.2 of etsi 119 472-3.

AS-AP-10-079.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-079.specification: The Wallet Unit SHALL present a different PID or attestation to each different Relying Party upon their request. This means that it SHALL comply with Method A for such Relying Parties.
AS-AP-10-079.searchText: issu_55 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit the wallet unit shall present a different pid or attestation to each different relying party upon their request. this means that it shall comply with method a for such relying parties.

AS-AP-10-080.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-080.specification: In case a given Relying Party requests attributes from a given type of PID or attestation multiple times, the Wallet Unit MAY present the same PID or attestation to this Relying Party each time. If it does, it SHALL comply with Method B or Method C for such a Relying Party.

AS-AP-10-084.subsection: E - HLRs for re-issuance and batch issuance of PIDs and attestations
AS-AP-10-084.specification: A Wallet Unit SHALL give its User the option to manually initiate a re-issuance process for any of the PIDs or attestations in their Wallet Unit.
AS-AP-10-084.notes: This requirement does not apply for WUAs, since Users must not be involved in the management of WUAs.
AS-AP-10-084.searchText: issu_58 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit a wallet unit shall give its user the option to manually initiate a re-issuance process for any of the pids or attestations in their wallet unit. this requirement does not apply for wuas, since users must not be involved in the management of wuas.

AS-AP-10-085.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-085.subsection: E - HLRs for re-issuance and batch issuance of PIDs and attestations
AS-AP-10-085.specification: After a successful re-issuance, a Wallet Unit SHALL compare the attribute values of the re-issued PID or attestation with those of the existing PID or attestation, and SHALL notify the User in case of any differences.
AS-AP-10-085.notes: This requirement does not apply for WUAs, since Users must not be involved in the management of WUAs.

AS-AP-10-086.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-086.subsection: E - HLRs for re-issuance and batch issuance of PIDs and attestations
AS-AP-10-086.specification: A Wallet Unit SHALL gracefully handle situations in which re-issuance of a PID, attestation, or WUA is refused by the PID Provider, Attestation Provider, or Wallet Provider,for example by attempting a retry after an appropriate delay.
AS-AP-10-086.searchText: issu_60 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit a wallet unit shall gracefully handle situations in which re-issuance of a pid, attestation, or wua is refused by the pid provider, attestation provider, or wallet provider,for example by attempting a retry after an appropriate delay.

AS-AP-10-087.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-087.subsection: E - HLRs for re-issuance and batch issuance of PIDs and attestations
AS-AP-10-087.specification: A Wallet Unit SHALL support PID or attestation first-time batch issuance with a single User authentication, regardless of the size of the batch.
AS-AP-10-087.notes: a) See also requirement WIAM_14. b) This requirement does not apply for WUAs, since Users must not be involved in the management of WUAs.

AS-AP-10-088.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-088.subsection: E - HLRs for re-issuance and batch issuance of PIDs and attestations
AS-AP-10-088.specification: If a PID or attestation was successfully re-issued because the value of one or more of its attributes was changed (including attributes being added or deleted), a Wallet Unit SHOULD delete the correct pre-existing PID or attestation.
AS-AP-10-088.notes: a) It is up to the Wallet Unit, possibly using metadata provided by the PID Provider or Attestation Provider using the [OpenID4VCI] protocol, to determine the PID or attestation to be deleted. b) Additionally, per requirement VCR_09, the PID Provider or Attestation Provider revokes the pre-existing PID or attestation.

AS-AP-10-089.subsection: E - HLRs for re-issuance and batch issuance of PIDs and attestations
AS-AP-10-089.specification: PID Providers and Attestation Providers, and Wallet Units SHALL support the features of [OpenID4VCI] enabling the re-issuance of PIDs and attestations.
AS-AP-10-089.searchText: issu_63 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit pid providers and attestation providers, and wallet units shall support the features of [openid4vci] enabling the re-issuance of pids and attestations.

AS-AP-10-090.specification: PID Providers, Attestation Providers, and Wallet Units SHALL support the features of [OpenID4VCI] enabling the batch issuance of PIDs or attestations.
AS-AP-10-090.searchText: issu_64 issuing a pid or attestation to a wallet unit pid providers, attestation providers, and wallet units shall support the features of [openid4vci] enabling the batch issuance of pids or attestations.

AS-AP-10-091.topicTitle: Issuing a PID or attestation to a Wallet Unit
AS-AP-10-091.subsection: E - HLRs for re-issuance and batch issuance of PIDs and attestations
AS-AP-10-091.specification: A PID Provider or an Attestation Provider of device-bound attestations SHALL verify that a re-issued PID or device-bound attestation is issued to the same Wallet Unit as the existing PID or attestation.
AS-AP-10-091.notes: A PID Provider or Attestation Provider can do so by issuing a refresh token to the Wallet Instance during the original issuance of the PID or attestation, and requiring that the Wallet Instance uses it to obtain a fresh access token during re-issuance; see [OpenID4VCI] section 14.5. The PID Provider or Attestation Provider needs to be able to trust that the Wallet Instance handles the refresh tokens in a secure way, so that an attacker cannot use them from another Wallet Instance. This requires trust in the (continued) security and integrity of both the original Wallet Instance and the other Wallet Instance. This trust is provided by providing the PID Provider or Attestation Provider with a valid WUA for the new Wallet Unit during re-issuance, and by enabling the PID Provider or Attestation Provider to verify that the existing Wallet Unit has not been revoked.

AS-WP-11-001.subsection: A. HLRs related to Use Cases A and B
AS-WP-11-001.specification: A Wallet Unit SHALL enable a User to generate a Pseudonym and register it at a Relying Party.
AS-WP-11-001.notes: For an attested pseudonym, pseudonym generation takes place by requesting the issuance of a pseudonym attestation. Pseudonym registration takes place by presenting the attestation.
AS-WP-11-001.searchText: pa_01 pseudonyms a wallet unit shall enable a user to generate a pseudonym and register it at a relying party. for an attested pseudonym, pseudonym generation takes place by requesting the issuance of a pseudonym attestation. pseudonym registration takes place by presenting the attestation.

AS-WP-11-002.subsection: A. HLRs related to Use Cases A and B
AS-WP-11-002.specification: A Wallet Unit SHALL enable a User to authenticate with a Pseudonym towards a Relying Party if the Wallet Unit was used previously to register the Pseudonym for the same Relying Party
AS-WP-11-002.searchText: pa_02 pseudonyms a wallet unit shall enable a user to authenticate with a pseudonym towards a relying party if the wallet unit was used previously to register the pseudonym for the same relying party

AS-WP-11-003.subsection: A. HLRs related to Use Cases A and B
AS-WP-11-003.specification: A Wallet Unit SHALL be able to perform the actions specified in the above two requirements independently of whether the interaction with the Relying Party is initiated on the same device hosting the Wallet Instance or on a device different from the one hosting the Wallet Instance.
AS-WP-11-003.searchText: pa_03 pseudonyms a wallet unit shall be able to perform the actions specified in the above two requirements independently of whether the interaction with the relying party is initiated on the same device hosting the wallet instance or on a device different from the one hosting the wallet instance.

AS-WP-11-004.subsection: A. HLRs related to Use Cases A and B
AS-WP-11-004.specification: A Wallet Unit SHALL enable the User to use multiple different Pseudonyms at a given Relying Party, unless it is explicitly designed as a scope rate-limited attestation.
AS-WP-11-004.searchText: pa_04 pseudonyms a wallet unit shall enable the user to use multiple different pseudonyms at a given relying party, unless it is explicitly designed as a scope rate-limited attestation.

AS-WP-11-005.subsection: A. HLRs related to Use Cases A and B
AS-WP-11-005.specification: A Wallet Unit SHOULD enable a User to freely choose a User alias for each Pseudonym registered at a Relying Party. Setting an alias SHOULD be optional for the User. The User SHOULD be able to change the alias for any Pseudonym.
AS-WP-11-005.searchText: pa_05 pseudonyms a wallet unit should enable a user to freely choose a user alias for each pseudonym registered at a relying party. setting an alias should be optional for the user. the user should be able to change the alias for any pseudonym.

AS-WP-11-006.subsection: A. HLRs related to Use Cases A and B
AS-WP-11-006.specification: A Wallet Unit SHALL enable a User to choose which Pseudonym to authenticate with towards a Relying Party, if multiple Pseudonyms are registered for this Relying Party. The Wallet Unit SHOULD present the User with the aliases of the applicable Pseudonyms, if assigned, when making this choice.
AS-WP-11-006.searchText: pa_06 pseudonyms a wallet unit shall enable a user to choose which pseudonym to authenticate with towards a relying party, if multiple pseudonyms are registered for this relying party. the wallet unit should present the user with the aliases of the applicable pseudonyms, if assigned, when making this choice.

AS-WP-11-007.subsection: A. HLRs related to Use Cases A and B
AS-WP-11-007.specification: A Wallet Unit SHALL enable a User to delete a Pseudonym.
AS-WP-11-007.searchText: pa_07 pseudonyms a wallet unit shall enable a user to delete a pseudonym.

AS-WP-11-008.subsection: A. HLRs related to Use Cases A and B
AS-WP-11-008.specification: A Wallet Unit SHALL enable the User to manage Pseudonyms within the Wallet Unit in a user-friendly and transparent manner.
AS-WP-11-008.searchText: pa_08 pseudonyms a wallet unit shall enable the user to manage pseudonyms within the wallet unit in a user-friendly and transparent manner.

AS-WP-11-009.subsection: A. HLRs related to Use Cases A and B
AS-WP-11-009.specification: A Wallet Unit SHALL log Pseudonym registration and presentation transactions as specified in [Topic 19](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/blob/v2.8.0/docs/annexes/annex-2/annex-2.02-high-level-requirements-by-topic.md#a2312-topic-19---user-navigation-requirements-dashboard-logs-for-transparency).
AS-WP-11-009.searchText: pa_08a pseudonyms a wallet unit shall log pseudonym registration and presentation transactions as specified in [topic 19](./annex-2.02-high-level-requirements-by-topic.md#a2312-topic-19---user-navigation-requirements-dashboard-logs-for-transparency).

AS-WP-11-010.subsection: A. HLRs related to Use Cases A and B
AS-WP-11-010.specification: A Wallet Unit SHALL enable the User to see all existing pseudonyms, including the associated Relying Party (if any).
AS-WP-11-010.searchText: pa_09 pseudonyms a wallet unit shall enable the user to see all existing pseudonyms, including the associated relying party (if any).

AS-WP-11-011.subsection: B. HLRs related to Relying Parties
AS-WP-11-011.specification: A Relying Party SHALL be able to verify that a User is registering a Pseudonym using a non-revoked Wallet Unit.
AS-WP-11-011.searchText: pa_10 pseudonyms a relying party shall be able to verify that a user is registering a pseudonym using a non-revoked wallet unit.

AS-WP-11-012.subsection: B. HLRs related to Relying Parties
AS-WP-11-012.specification: A Relying Party SHALL be able to verify that a User is authenticating with a Pseudonym using a non-revoked Wallet Unit.
AS-WP-11-012.searchText: pa_11 pseudonyms a relying party shall be able to verify that a user is authenticating with a pseudonym using a non-revoked wallet unit.

AS-WP-11-013.subsection: B. HLRs related to Relying Parties
AS-WP-11-013.specification: If Wallet Unit is used to register a Pseudonym at a Relying Party in combination with a PID or attestation being presented to the same Relying Party, then this Relying Party SHALL be able to verify that the same User performed both actions.
AS-WP-11-013.searchText: pa_12 pseudonyms if wallet unit is used to register a pseudonym at a relying party in combination with a pid or attestation being presented to the same relying party, then this relying party shall be able to verify that the same user performed both actions.

AS-WP-11-014.subsection: B. HLRs related to Relying Parties
AS-WP-11-014.specification: The Relying Party SHALL be able to validate that the pseudonym presented to them belongs to the User presenting it.
AS-WP-11-014.searchText: pa_13 pseudonyms the relying party shall be able to validate that the pseudonym presented to them belongs to the user presenting it.

AS-WP-11-015.specification: A Wallet Unit SHALL store the information necessary for authenticating with a Pseudonym in either a WSCA/WSCD or in a keystore.
AS-WP-11-015.searchText: pa_14 pseudonyms a wallet unit shall store the information necessary for authenticating with a pseudonym in either a wsca/wscd or in a keystore.

AS-WP-11-016.specification: A Relying Party SHALL NOT be able to derive the User's true identity, or any data identifying the User, from the Pseudonym value received by the Relying Party.
AS-WP-11-016.searchText: pa_15 pseudonyms a relying party shall not be able to derive the user's true identity, or any data identifying the user, from the pseudonym value received by the relying party.

AS-WP-11-017.specification: A Wallet Unit SHALL NOT reveal the same Pseudonym to different Relying Parties, unless the User explicitly chooses otherwise.
AS-WP-11-017.searchText: pa_16 pseudonyms a wallet unit shall not reveal the same pseudonym to different relying parties, unless the user explicitly chooses otherwise.

AS-WP-11-018.specification: It SHALL NOT be possible to correlate Pseudonyms based on their values nor on other metadata sent by the Wallet Unit during registration and authentication, meaning that colluding Relying Parties SHALL NOT able to conclude that different Pseudonyms belong to the same User.
AS-WP-11-018.searchText: pa_17 pseudonyms it shall not be possible to correlate pseudonyms based on their values nor on other metadata sent by the wallet unit during registration and authentication, meaning that colluding relying parties shall not able to conclude that different pseudonyms belong to the same user.

AS-WP-11-019.specification: The Wallet Unit SHALL ensure that Pseudonyms contain sufficient entropy to make the chance of colliding Pseudonyms (meaning two Users having the same Pseudonym value for the same Relying Party) negligible.
AS-WP-11-019.searchText: pa_18 pseudonyms the wallet unit shall ensure that pseudonyms contain sufficient entropy to make the chance of colliding pseudonyms (meaning two users having the same pseudonym value for the same relying party) negligible.

AS-WP-11-020.specification: A Wallet Unit SHALL NOT share the User's optionally assigned Pseudonym aliases with any Relying Party.
AS-WP-11-020.searchText: pa_19 pseudonyms a wallet unit shall not share the user's optionally assigned pseudonym aliases with any relying party.

AS-WP-11-021.specification: The Wallet Unit SHALL verify the identity of a Relying Party when a User registers a Pseudonym or authenticates with a Pseudonym. If the profile or extension of [W3C WebAuthn] meant in PA_21 does not enable the Wallet Unit to do this, the Wallet Unit SHALL trust the WebAuthn Client (i.e., the browser) to verify the Relying Party identity.
AS-WP-11-021.notes: [W3C WebAuthn] currently does not offer a way for an Authenticator (i.e., the Wallet Unit) to authenticate a Relying Party. Instead, the Client (i.e., the browser) will authenticate the Relying Party, using TLS.
AS-WP-11-021.searchText: pa_20 pseudonyms the wallet unit shall verify the identity of a relying party when a user registers a pseudonym or authenticates with a pseudonym. if the profile or extension of [w3c webauthn] meant in pa_21 does not enable the wallet unit to do this, the wallet unit shall trust the webauthn client (i.e., the browser) to verify the relying party identity. [w3c webauthn] currently does not offer a way for an authenticator (i.e., the wallet unit) to authenticate a relying party. instead, the client (i.e., the browser) will authenticate the relying party, using tls.

AS-WP-11-022.specification: The Commission SHALL create or reference a technical specification containing a profile or extension of the [W3C WebAuthn] specification compliant with the HLRs specified in this Topic. This specification SHALL contain all details necessary for Wallet Units and Relying Parties to generate, register, and use Pseudonyms.
AS-WP-11-022.searchText: pa_21 pseudonyms the commission shall create or reference a technical specification containing a profile or extension of the [w3c webauthn] specification compliant with the hlrs specified in this topic. this specification shall contain all details necessary for wallet units and relying parties to generate, register, and use pseudonyms.

AS-WP-11-023.specification: Wallet Providers MAY ensure that their Wallet Solution supports the HLRs defined for this topic by letting their Wallet Units perform the role of a WebAuthn authenticator following the [W3C WebAuthn] specification and the technical specification referenced in referenced in PA_21.
AS-WP-11-023.searchText: pa_22 pseudonyms wallet providers may ensure that their wallet solution supports the hlrs defined for this topic by letting their wallet units perform the role of a webauthn authenticator following the [w3c webauthn] specification and the technical specification referenced in referenced in pa_21.

AS-WP-11-024.subsection: E. HLRs related to scope rate-limited pseudonyms
AS-WP-11-024.specification: A protocol enabling scope rate-limited pseudonyms SHALL rely solely on algorithms included in the [ECCG Agreed Cryptographic Mechanisms v2.0](https://certification.enisa.europa.eu/document/download/a845662b-aee0-484e-9191-890c4cfa7aaa_en?filename=ECCG%20Agreed%20Cryptographic%20Mechanisms%20version%202.pdf).
AS-WP-11-024.searchText: pa_23 pseudonyms a protocol enabling scope rate-limited pseudonyms shall rely solely on algorithms included in the [eccg agreed cryptographic mechanisms v2.0](https://certification.enisa.europa.eu/document/download/a845662b-aee0-484e-9191-890c4cfa7aaa_en?filename=eccg%20agreed%20cryptographic%20mechanisms%20version%202.pdf).

AS-WP-11-025.subsection: E. HLRs related to scope rate-limited pseudonyms
AS-WP-11-025.specification: A protocol enabling scope rate-limited pseudonyms SHALL enable a Wallet Unit to allow a User to generate a scope rate-limited pseudonym, register this by a Relying Party, and prove that this is within the rate and scope restrictions determined by the Relying Party.
AS-WP-11-025.searchText: pa_24 pseudonyms a protocol enabling scope rate-limited pseudonyms shall enable a wallet unit to allow a user to generate a scope rate-limited pseudonym, register this by a relying party, and prove that this is within the rate and scope restrictions determined by the relying party.

AS-WP-11-026.subsection: E. HLRs related to scope rate-limited pseudonyms
AS-WP-11-026.specification: A protocol enabling scope rate-limited pseudonyms SHALL allow a Relying Party, when a User presents a scope rate-limited pseudonym, to verify that the rate is not exceeded for this User.
AS-WP-11-026.searchText: pa_25 pseudonyms a protocol enabling scope rate-limited pseudonyms shall allow a relying party, when a user presents a scope rate-limited pseudonym, to verify that the rate is not exceeded for this user.

AS-WP-11-027.subsection: E. HLRs related to scope rate-limited pseudonyms
AS-WP-11-027.specification: A protocol enabling scope rate-limited pseudonyms SHALL allow a Relying Party to choose the scope and rate when requesting a scope rate-limited pseudonym from a User.
AS-WP-11-027.searchText: pa_26 pseudonyms a protocol enabling scope rate-limited pseudonyms shall allow a relying party to choose the scope and rate when requesting a scope rate-limited pseudonym from a user.

AS-WP-11-028.subsection: E. HLRs related to scope rate-limited pseudonyms
AS-WP-11-028.specification: A protocol enabling scope rate-limited pseudonyms SHALL NOT allow any entity or collusion of entities not including the User, to link scope rate-limited pseudonyms of the same User when used across several different Relying Parties. This SHALL hold even if the scope and rate are identical across the different Relying Parties and both for registration and authentication of the scope rate-limited pseudonym
AS-WP-11-028.searchText: pa_27 pseudonyms a protocol enabling scope rate-limited pseudonyms shall not allow any entity or collusion of entities not including the user, to link scope rate-limited pseudonyms of the same user when used across several different relying parties. this shall hold even if the scope and rate are identical across the different relying parties and both for registration and authentication of the scope rate-limited pseudonym

AS-WP-11-029.subsection: E. HLRs related to scope rate-limited pseudonyms
AS-WP-11-029.specification: A protocol enabling scope rate-limited pseudonyms SHALL ensure that if the rate is larger than 1, a User's different pseudonyms SHALL be unlinkable for the same scope. This SHALL hold against any entity or collusion of entities, not including the User. Further, such protocol SHALL ensure that during registration or authentication with such a pseudonym, it SHALL NOT be possible for the Relying Party to deduce any information about how many pseudonyms the User has already registered (except that it does not exceed the predetermined rate).
AS-WP-11-029.searchText: pa_28 pseudonyms a protocol enabling scope rate-limited pseudonyms shall ensure that if the rate is larger than 1, a user's different pseudonyms shall be unlinkable for the same scope. this shall hold against any entity or collusion of entities, not including the user. further, such protocol shall ensure that during registration or authentication with such a pseudonym, it shall not be possible for the relying party to deduce any information about how many pseudonyms the user has already registered (except that it does not exceed the predetermined rate).

AS-WP-11-030.subsection: E. HLRs related to scope rate-limited pseudonyms
AS-WP-11-030.specification: A protocol enabling scope rate-limited pseudonyms SHALL ensure that no entity or collusion of entities, not including a User, is able to authenticate or register with a scope rate-limited pseudonym of this User.
AS-WP-11-030.searchText: pa_29 pseudonyms a protocol enabling scope rate-limited pseudonyms shall ensure that no entity or collusion of entities, not including a user, is able to authenticate or register with a scope rate-limited pseudonym of this user.

AS-WP-11-031.subsection: E. HLRs related to scope rate-limited pseudonyms
AS-WP-11-031.specification: A Wallet Unit SHALL store cryptographic material necessary for authenticating as a scope rate-limited pseudonyms in either a WSCA/WSCD or in a keystore.
AS-WP-11-031.searchText: pa_30 pseudonyms a wallet unit shall store cryptographic material necessary for authenticating as a scope rate-limited pseudonyms in either a wsca/wscd or in a keystore.

AS-WP-11-032.subsection: E. HLRs related to scope rate-limited pseudonyms
AS-WP-11-032.specification: A User's scope rate limited pseudonyms for a particular scope and rate SHALL be persistent over time even if they start using another Wallet Unit.
AS-WP-11-032.searchText: pa_31 pseudonyms a user's scope rate limited pseudonyms for a particular scope and rate shall be persistent over time even if they start using another wallet unit.

AS-AP-12-001.specification: The Scheme Provider for an Attestation Rulebook describing a type of attestation that is a QEAA or a PuB-EAA SHALL specify that one or more of the following two common format(s) must be used for these attestations: - The format specified in ISO/IEC 18013-5, see [ISO18013-5]. - The format specified in SD-JWT-based Verifiable Credentials (SD-JWT VC), see [SD-JWT-VC].
AS-AP-12-001.searchText: arb_01 attestation rulebooks the scheme provider for an attestation rulebook describing a type of attestation that is a qeaa or a pub-eaa shall specify that one or more of the following two common format(s) must be used for these attestations: - the format specified in iso/iec 18013-5, see [iso18013-5]. - the format specified in sd-jwt-based verifiable credentials (sd-jwt vc), see [sd-jwt-vc].

EW-DM-12-001.specification: The Scheme Provider for an Attestation Rulebook describing a type of attestation that is a non-qualified EAA SHALL specify that one or more of the following three common format(s) must be used for these attestations: - The format specified in ISO/IEC 18013-5, see [ISO18013-5]. - The format specified in SD-JWT-based Verifiable Credentials (SD-JWT VC), see [SD-JWT-VC]. - The format specified in W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model, see [W3C VCDM v2.0].
EW-DM-12-001.searchText: arb_01a attestation rulebooks the scheme provider for an attestation rulebook describing a type of attestation that is a non-qualified eaa shall specify that one or more of the following three common format(s) must be used for these attestations: - the format specified in iso/iec 18013-5, see [iso18013-5]. - the format specified in sd-jwt-based verifiable credentials (sd-jwt vc), see [sd-jwt-vc]. - the format specified in w3c verifiable credentials data model, see [w3c vcdm v2.0].

EW-DM-12-002.specification: The Scheme Provider for an Attestation Rulebook describing attestations using the format specified in [SD-JWT VC] SHALL ensure that these attestations comply with the 'IETF SD-JWT VC Profile' specified in [HAIP] Section 6.1.
EW-DM-12-002.searchText: arb_01b attestation rulebooks the scheme provider for an attestation rulebook describing attestations using the format specified in [sd-jwt vc] shall ensure that these attestations comply with the 'ietf sd-jwt vc profile' specified in [haip] section 6.1.

EW-DM-12-003.specification: The Scheme Provider for an Attestation Rulebook SHALL analyse whether it must be possible for a User to present that type of attestation when the Wallet Unit and the Relying Party are in proximity and attestations are presented without using the internet. If so, the Attestation Rulebook SHALL specify that the attestations must be issued in the ISO/IEC 18013-5-compliant mdoc format.
EW-DM-12-003.notes: In theory, it is possible to use SD-JWT VC-compliant attestations in proximity use cases. In practice, however, the only protocol available to request and present SD-JWT VC-compliant attestations between a Wallet Unit and a Relying Party Instance is OpenID4VP. That protocol cannot be used without internet connectivity.
EW-DM-12-003.searchText: arb_02 attestation rulebooks the scheme provider for an attestation rulebook shall analyse whether it must be possible for a user to present that type of attestation when the wallet unit and the relying party are in proximity and attestations are presented without using the internet. if so, the attestation rulebook shall specify that the attestations must be issued in the iso/iec 18013-5-compliant mdoc format. in theory, it is possible to use sd-jwt vc-compliant attestations in proximity use cases. in practice, however, the only protocol available to request and present sd-jwt vc-compliant attestations between a wallet unit and a relying party instance is openid4vp. that protocol cannot be used without internet connectivity.

EW-DM-12-004.specification: The Scheme Provider for an Attestation Rulebook MAY specify in the Attestation Rulebook that that type of attestation must be issued in the [SD-JWT VC]-compliant format, provided the [SD-JWT VC] specification has been approved by an EU standardisation body or by the European Digital Identity Cooperation Group established pursuant to [Article 46e](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=CELEX:32024R1183#d1e4536-1-1)(1) of the [European Digital Identity Regulation].
EW-DM-12-004.searchText: arb_03 attestation rulebooks the scheme provider for an attestation rulebook may specify in the attestation rulebook that that type of attestation must be issued in the [sd-jwt vc]-compliant format, provided the [sd-jwt vc] specification has been approved by an eu standardisation body or by the european digital identity cooperation group established pursuant to [article 46e](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/en/all/?uri=celex:32024r1183#d1e4536-1-1)(1) of the [european digital identity regulation].

EW-DM-12-005.specification: If an Attestation Rulebook specifies that a type of attestation can be issued in a format compliant with [W3C VCDM v2.0], the Scheme Provider for that Attestation Rulebook SHALL ensure the Rulebook references one or more documents specifying in detail how a Relying Party can request attributes from a such an attestation, and how a User can selectively disclose attributes from such an attestation. Moreover, these referenced documents SHALL be approved by an EU standardisation body or by the European Digital Identity Cooperation Group established pursuant to [Article 46e](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=CELEX:32024R1183#d1e4536-1-1)(1) of the [European Digital Identity Regulation].
EW-DM-12-005.searchText: arb_04 attestation rulebooks if an attestation rulebook specifies that a type of attestation can be issued in a format compliant with [w3c vcdm v2.0], the scheme provider for that attestation rulebook shall ensure the rulebook references one or more documents specifying in detail how a relying party can request attributes from a such an attestation, and how a user can selectively disclose attributes from such an attestation. moreover, these referenced documents shall be approved by an eu standardisation body or by the european digital identity cooperation group established pursuant to [article 46e](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/en/all/?uri=celex:32024r1183#d1e4536-1-1)(1) of the [european digital identity regulation].

EW-DM-12-006.specification: The Scheme Provider for an Attestation Rulebook SHALL specify a value for the attestation type, which SHALL be unique within the scope of the EUDI Wallet ecosystem.
EW-DM-12-006.notes: In ISO/IEC 18013-5, the attestation type is called 'document type' and is included as a ``docType`` key-value pair in both the mdoc request and the mdoc response. Also, a method for generating unique attestation type values is recommended. In OpenID4VP, the attestation type is included in the meta property of a Credential Query in a presentation request. In [SD-JWT VC], the attestation type is called 'SD-JWT VC type' and is included as a ``vct`` claim in the SD-JWT VC.
EW-DM-12-006.searchText: arb_05 attestation rulebooks the scheme provider for an attestation rulebook shall specify a value for the attestation type, which shall be unique within the scope of the eudi wallet ecosystem. in iso/iec 18013-5, the attestation type is called 'document type' and is included as a ``doctype`` key-value pair in both the mdoc request and the mdoc response. also, a method for generating unique attestation type values is recommended. in openid4vp, the attestation type is included in the meta property of a credential query in a presentation request. in [sd-jwt vc], the attestation type is called 'sd-jwt vc type' and is included as a ``vct`` claim in the sd-jwt vc.

EW-DM-12-007.specification: The Scheme Provider for an Attestation Rulebook SHALL define all attributes that an attestation of that type may contain. This definition SHALL first describe the semantics of each attribute in an encoding-independent manner and SHALL subsequently for each attribute specify an ISO/IEC 18013-5-compliant format, an SD-JWT VC-compliant format, or both, as needed given the choices made according to ARB_01 - ARB_04.
EW-DM-12-007.searchText: arb_06 attestation rulebooks the scheme provider for an attestation rulebook shall define all attributes that an attestation of that type may contain. this definition shall first describe the semantics of each attribute in an encoding-independent manner and shall subsequently for each attribute specify an iso/iec 18013-5-compliant format, an sd-jwt vc-compliant format, or both, as needed given the choices made according to arb_01 - arb_04.

EW-DM-12-008.specification: For ISO/IEC 18013-5-compliant attestations, the Attestation Rulebook SHALL define each attribute within an attribute namespace. An attribute namespace SHALL fully define the identifier, the syntax, and the semantics of each attribute within that namespace. An attribute namespace SHALL have an identifier that is unique within the scope of the EUDI Wallet ecosystem, and each attribute identifier SHALL be unique within that namespace.
EW-DM-12-008.notes: In ISO/IEC 18013-5, namespaces are discussed and a method for generating unique namespace identifiers is recommended.
EW-DM-12-008.searchText: arb_06a attestation rulebooks for iso/iec 18013-5-compliant attestations, the attestation rulebook shall define each attribute within an attribute namespace. an attribute namespace shall fully define the identifier, the syntax, and the semantics of each attribute within that namespace. an attribute namespace shall have an identifier that is unique within the scope of the eudi wallet ecosystem, and each attribute identifier shall be unique within that namespace. in iso/iec 18013-5, namespaces are discussed and a method for generating unique namespace identifiers is recommended.

EW-DM-12-009.specification: For [SD-JWT VC]-compliant attestations, the Scheme Provider for the Attestation Rulebook SHALL ensure that each claim name is either: - included in the IANA registry for JWT claims, - is a Public Name as defined in [RFC 7519], or is a Private Name specific to the attestation type.
EW-DM-12-009.notes: [SD-JWT VC] does not discuss how to avoid conflicting claim names. Since SD-JWTs are a special kind of JWTs, the methods specified in RFC 7519 are applicable.
EW-DM-12-009.searchText: arb_06b attestation rulebooks for [sd-jwt vc]-compliant attestations, the scheme provider for the attestation rulebook shall ensure that each claim name is either: - included in the iana registry for jwt claims, - is a public name as defined in [rfc 7519], or is a private name specific to the attestation type. [sd-jwt vc] does not discuss how to avoid conflicting claim names. since sd-jwts are a special kind of jwts, the methods specified in rfc 7519 are applicable.

EW-DM-12-010.specification: When determining the attributes to be included in a new attestation type, the Scheme Provider for the applicable Attestation Rulebook SHOULD consider referring to attributes that are already included in the catalogue of attributes specified in [Topic 25](https://github.com/eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/blob/v2.8.0/docs/annexes/annex-2/annex-2.02-high-level-requirements-by-topic.md#a2315-topic-25---unified-definition-and-controlled-vocabularies-for-attributes) or specified in an attestation scheme included in the catalogue of attestation schemes specified in [Commission Implementing Regulation 2025/1569](http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg_impl/2025/1569/oj), rather than unnecessarily re-defining all attributes.
EW-DM-12-010.searchText: arb_07 attestation rulebooks when determining the attributes to be included in a new attestation type, the scheme provider for the applicable attestation rulebook should consider referring to attributes that are already included in the catalogue of attributes specified in [topic 25](./annex-2.02-high-level-requirements-by-topic.md#a2315-topic-25---unified-definition-and-controlled-vocabularies-for-attributes) or specified in an attestation scheme included in the catalogue of attestation schemes specified in [commission implementing regulation 2025/1569](http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg_impl/2025/1569/oj), rather than unnecessarily re-defining all attributes.
